title: Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten

issues.location: sections/transcripts.tex, Definition def:protocol and Lemma lem:transcript (measurable / countable-schedule case)
issues.description: The admitted-protocol model for countable or measurable schedules is nonstandard and heavy. It includes reference-compatibility and terminal-readout clauses, so the K_D=0 statement for infinite protocols holds only inside this model as the paper defines it. This is not an error: for ordinary finite-round LOCC, the product form X_i(t) ⊗ Y_j(t) at each transcript is standard and clearly correct.
issues.evidence: In the finite-record subsection, the branch for transcript t and bits (i,j) is A_i^t ⊗ B_j^t, because the private histories sum independently in each laboratory once t is fixed. The general case relies on probe-and-filter arguments plus extension theorems that depend on clauses 5 and 6 of the definition.

coverage: Read in full: introduction, foundations, coherence, transcripts, secret-key, geometry, certificate and applications. Did not read the projection and combinatorial sections (an independent second construction, not needed for the main theorems) or the algebra appendix in detail. Checked by hand: Lemma 3.2 (positive block), the four-effect inequality including both block bounds, the transpose identities and the spectral split; the Choi transfer and class-C membership; the fidelity identity for Eve's blocks and the Powers–Størmer lower bound; e ≤ η/2, f ≥ (1−η)/2, and the 2/5 threshold that gives the 1/5 gap; the finite-transcript product structure; the Kraus form and PPT property of L; the exterior-square kernel argument and the 9+9<20 exclusion; the logic of the Frobenius cycle types (1,2,17) and (1,19) giving S20 and transport to every 10-subset; and the trace-preserving channel completion (F_i ⪰ c_i I, the composed corner equals c1c2 Ψ2Ψ1). Re-ran exact_certificate.py; its output matches the recorded output byte for byte. Used the sibling's numerical checks (20 points, all C(20,10) determinants, rank of Z).
main_claim: There is an explicit entangled state ρ = Z/tr Z on C^10 ⊗ C^10, where Z = J(Φ2∘Φ1) for PPT maps Φ1, Φ2. The range of ρ contains no product vector, K_D(ρ)=0, and every admitted protocol misses an ideal secret bit by at least 1/5 in trace norm. Corollaries: a counterexample to the two-map PPT² conjecture, and a 21-dimensional trace-preserving PPT channel whose square is not entanglement breaking.
sibling_notes: An earlier branch had already posted no_gap_found for this same directory with numerical checks. This second pass agrees, after independently re-deriving the coherence inequality, the secret-bit gap, the transcript factorization, the tensor-geometry step and the channel completion, and replaying the certificate.
